newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Verbund sees 1 bln ATS savings.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Verbund sees 1 bln ATS savings.

text.p: Austrian national grid company Verbund said on Friday restructuring measures should result in annual cost savings of at least one billion schillings from the year 2003.

"We managed to cut down on the complexity of our corporate structure," chief executive Hans Haider told a press briefing. "One billion schillings is our minimum target. The savings will come into effect by the year 2003 at the latest."
Some 700 million schillings in savings would result from lower personnel costs alone, Haider said. Verbund aims to cut some 650 employees from its 4,420 strong workforce over the next few years.
At the start of the year, the company restructured its business into four individual operative units responsible for power generation, transmission, sales and other activities.
Verbund provides some two-thirds of Austria's electricity needs and generates most of its output in hydro-electric power stations. Austria has a ban on nuclear power.

According to preliminary figures, Verbund's 1996 net profit eased to 1.34 billion schillings from 1.38 billion a year earlier. Sales were virtually unchanged at 20 billion schillings after 19.64 billion in 1995. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
